English: Wayfarers Hut
A rudimentary shelter, little more than a hide tent with a communal fire, for passing travelers and the occasional lost soul.
Pilgrims Shelter
A larger tented structure with mats and modest provisions, offering warmth and protection to Christian pilgrims journeying across the wild steppe.
Rest Chamber
A wooden or felt-walled communal chamber, with small cots and a guarded entry, allowing pilgrims a more secure and restful stay.
Guarded Pavilion
A robust tented complex with a wooden palisade and stationed guards, providing protection and organization for itinerant Christians.
Hospitality Room
A permanent wooden structure with proper bedding, communal kitchens, and a prayer alcove, ensuring comfort, safety, and spiritual solace.
Guesthouse
A large, multi-roomed guesthouse with private quarters for dignitaries, storerooms, and an attached chapel, attracting pilgrims from afar.
Sanctuary Hall
A well-defended hall with stone foundations, separate wings for the sick and honored, and a consecrated sanctuary for worship and reflection.
Refuge Pavilion
An ornate but sturdy compound, with stone and timber, providing refuge to large numbers of pilgrims and clanfolk, with stores for food and water.
Grand Pilgrims Hostel
A sprawling complex of halls, chapels, and barracks, replete with gardens, libraries, and sacred relics. The center for Christian unity and rest upon the steppes.
Christian Pilgrim Hostel
A legendary center of faith, hospitality, and pilgrimage, known throughout Christendom for its sanctuary, its wonders, and its protection for all who journey in the Lords name.
